a: A Vivid Vision is a detailed picture of your business and your life three years from now, written in the present tense as if it has already happened. It uses plain language and word-pictures so anyone on your team can read it and see the same future you see.

q: How is a Vivid Vision different from a business plan or a vision board?
a: A business plan is mostly numbers and how-to. A vision board is mostly pictures with no plan behind it. A Vivid Vision sits in between. It describes what the company looks like, sounds like, and feels like in three years, in enough detail that your team can act on it, and it covers your life, not just the business.

q: Why three years and not one year or ten?
a: One year is too close to feel big. Ten years is too far to feel real. Three years is far enough to dream past your current constraints and close enough that you can start building toward it on Monday.

q: Do I write it about my business, my life, or both?
a: Both, in one document. Most planning splits them apart, which is why neither one sticks. When you build them together, every business decision starts moving you toward the life you actually want.

q: How long does it take to create one?
a: The first draft can come out of a focused two-day process or a VIP day. Refining the language and designing the final document takes a few more weeks. Then the real work is the rollout to your team.

q: What happens after it is written? How do I roll it out to my team?
a: The Vivid Vision is not a document for your wall. You share it with your team, your investors, and sometimes your closest clients. You read it out loud, you hand out copies, and you let people raise their hand for the parts they want to own.

q: My team is remote. Does this still work?
a: Yes. Some of the strongest rollouts have been remote teams who received a printed vision packet in the mail and opened it together on a call. The point is that everyone sees the same picture at the same time.

q: I have done goal-setting retreats before and nothing stuck. Why is this different?
a: Most retreats send you home with a list of goals and no picture and no rollout. A Vivid Vision gives you a picture your team can see, a plan to build it, and a rhythm to keep it in front of you. The rollout is the part almost everyone skips, and it is the part that makes it stick.

q: Who is this for, and who is it not for?
a: It is for founders and CEOs who have a real business and a team and want a clear picture of where they are taking both the company and their life. It is not for someone looking for a quick hack, or someone who is not willing to step away from the daily grind long enough to think.

q: What is the difference between Done-For-You, the Retreat, and the Quest course?
a: Done-For-You means the team clarifies, writes, and designs your Vivid Vision for you. The Retreat is an in-person experience where you build it in a room with other founders. The Vision Driven Quest is an online course where you build it yourself at your own pace.
It is a 15-minute daily guided breathwork practice for staying connected to your vision. A vision you look at once a year does not change your decisions. A daily practice keeps it live.

q: How do I know if I am achievement-driven or vision-driven right now?
a: Achievement-driven means you are chasing the next milestone and the win never feels like enough. Vision-driven means your daily decisions are guided by a clear picture of the life and business you want. Most founders are stuck in the first stage and have never been shown the second.

q: Can I do this if my business is under $1M in revenue?
a: Yes. The process works at any size. It matters most once you have a team, because that is when a shared picture of the future starts saving you from making every decision yourself.

q: What results do founders actually see after doing this?
a: It varies. Founders have reported revenue and profit growth, a team that makes decisions without them, and time back with their family during seasons they used to miss. Results are never guaranteed, and anyone who guarantees them is not being straight with you.
